verdict: Real import-capable OpenTofu provider works for bytes-preserving adoption and guarded disposal, but forced replacement can destroy a retained artifact before creation fails.

evidence.kind: Actual compiled Go provider and local OpenTofu CLI; no surrogate or simulation
passed_probes: content mismatch rejected on refresh and deletion
actual SIGKILL after unlink and safe retry
evidence.counterexample: apply -replace=immutable_artifact.result unlinks the valid file, then fails adoption-only Create

limitations: No apply-time retirement admission token or retention gate
Ownership labels are not exclusive or authenticated
Conditional path unlink remains racy under hostile external namespace mutation
No erasure or power-loss durability guarantee
next_experiment: Integrate journal-backed destructive authorization in Delete and saved-plan admission; reject forced replacement and duplicate adoption while preserving retry after unlink/acknowledgement interruption.
docs: Context7 monthly quota exceeded; pinned official SDK source and official OpenTofu documentation used directly.
